title: IT-Systemadministrator
description:
Wir sind ein inhabergeführtes IT-Systemhaus in Chemnitz und betreuen seit 2016 die IT von Geschäftskunden - vom Arbeitsplatz über Microsoft 365 und Server bis zu Netzwerk, Security und Cloud.
Wir suchen jemanden für den First und Second Level Support unserer Kunden. Nicht als Dauerposition am unteren Ende einer Support-Pyramide, sondern als Einstieg, aus dem sich in den nächsten Jahren eigene Kunden und eigene Fachthemen entwickeln sollen.
Was dieser Job ist, steht unten. Was er nicht ist, auch.
Aufgaben

Du nimmst Störungen unserer Geschäftskunden an - per Telefon, per Remote-Support und bei Bedarf vor Ort beim Kunden.
Du analysierst, priorisierst und löst eigenständig: Arbeitsplätze, Windows Clients und Server, Microsoft 365, Benutzer und Berechtigungen, Netzwerk, Drucker, Software, sonstige Infrastruktur.
Du dokumentierst nachvollziehbar im Ticketsystem. Nicht für die Statistik, sondern damit die Kollegin oder der Kollege nach dir nicht bei null anfängt.
Du kommunizierst mit Anwendern, die keine IT-Leute sind - verständlich und ohne sie dumm dastehen zu lassen.
Wenn du nicht weiterkommst, eskalierst du an unsere Engineers. Aber vollständig: Fehlerbild, deine Analyse, was du schon probiert hast.

Wie sich das entwickelt
Bei uns ist First Level kein Endzustand.
Je sicherer du in einem Thema wirst, desto mehr davon bekommst du. Konkret heißt das: zuerst einzelne Second-Level-Themen, dann Verantwortung für feste Kunden, dann ein eigener technischer Schwerpunkt - zum Beispiel Netzwerk, Microsoft 365, Server, Firewall oder Cloud.
Wie schnell das geht, hängt an dir, nicht an einer Beförderungsstufe im Organigramm. Wer zuverlässig arbeitet, bekommt bei uns mehr Entscheidungsspielraum, nicht mehr Kontrolle. Welche Weiterbildung du machst, besprechen wir nach Bedarf und Interesse, nicht nach Katalog.

title: Head of Applied AI
description:
Head of Applied AI

Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Defence/SC Clearance Requirements:

SC clearance is required for our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. DV clearance may be required for certain roles, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

About Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. We partner with ambitious enterprise and public sector customers to design, build, operate, and support secure, governed cloud platforms that meet the highest regulatory and industry standards.

We are scaling deliberately. Our revenue ambition depends on deploying the right people onto the right work quickly, and on making disciplined use of our capacity. This role is central to that.

 

About the role

Cloudscaler's Applied AI business unit launched at the start of 2026 and has grown quickly, with an established offering, live client engagements and a pipeline in place. The current Head of Applied AI is stepping back from the role for personal reasons and remains with the business to hand over, so the incoming Head inherits a running unit rather than a standing start. We are recruiting to take it into its next phase of growth.

The work is running; the structure is not yet. Offerings are defined, collateral exists, engagements are live and Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI is established. What does not yet exist is the shape around it: there is no ring-fenced team, no separate P&L and no formally defined roles. The unit began with strategy, technical expertise and sales all held in one place. Technical capability has grown since; strategy and commercial ownership have not. Formalising the practice - defining the team, the roles and the commercial structure - is part of the job rather than something the incoming Head inherits finished.

This role has both external and internal responsibilities:

Externally, it owns our AI go-to-market offerings and the customer, partner and pre-sales activity that turns them into pipeline, and it is Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI.

Internally, it carries full commercial accountability for the business unit, provides technical delivery oversight, builds and leads the practice, and is accountable for enabling the whole company to work with AI.

The role reports to the CTO and works closely with leadership across the business. The person needs to be technical enough to direct and challenge the engineering work, and commercially credible enough to scale the unit and its offering.

It is a hands-on role. In one week, you might write a business case for the Leadership Team, advise a client CTO on their AI strategy, review an engineer's architecture decision and speak at a conference on what we have learned.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp already serves thousands of organizations in industries where financial operations work differently: construction companies that manage spend by job and cost code, nonprofits that report by fund and grant, and public-sector organizations accountable for every taxpayer dollar.

We are hiring a Lead Product Marketing Manager, Verticals to turn those differences into a durable growth advantage.

title: UI/UX Designer (12 mos. Contract)
description:
Reports to: Creative Lead
Location: Remote (U.S. or Canada); West Coast preferred or PST hours required.

About the Role

NETGEAR (Consumer division) is building an in-house creative team to own digital design work end to end. The team is small on purpose: a Creative Lead, a UI Designer, a Graphic Designer, and a copywriter.

This is the digital design seat, focused on the direct-to-consumer side of netgear.com http://netgear.com. It is a transactional storefront, so the work carries real conversion pressure. You will design and ship interface work for web, working inside an established atomic design system rather than starting from a blank canvas each time.

Our team owns the web UI system. You will be the person working in it day to day: building with it, extending it, and keeping it coherent as the site grows.

You will have access to website analytics and performance data, and you will work alongside our Lead of Consumer Insights, whose findings should feed directly into design decisions. Your job is to take what all of that tells us and make it show up in the interface.

Working inside an established system does not mean only assembling from what already exists. We expect you to spot where the system falls short of what a page actually needs, and to design new components that fit the existing logic rather than working around it.

Our app is owned by a separate product team. You will not design app screens, but you will work with them to keep web and app visually consistent.

What you will do

- Design and ship UI across the consumer side of netgear.com http://netgear.com, from wireframe through to developer-ready handoff. The work spans campaign and product landing pages, category and listing pages, product detail pages, media and content pages, and the interface for our product finder tools.

- Work in our atomic web design system: build with existing components, extend it where the system does not yet cover what a page needs, and keep new work consistent with what is already there.

- Maintain our web Figma libraries, keeping components, variants, and tokens clean, documented, and usable by everyone touching the files.

- Work with the front-end team who build and own the website itself: hand off designs in a state they can implement, check feasibility before committing to an approach, and review designs in staging before they go live.

- Use website analytics and consumer insights research as inputs to design decisions.

- Design new web components and suggest design improvements to our pages.

- Collaborate with the Graphic Designer so that campaign work and site experience feel like the same brand.

- Work closely with our Sr. Integrated Marketing Manager, who is responsible for global campaigns, so that site work lines up with what campaigns are driving.

- Use AI tools as part of your workflow where they genuinely speed things up.

- Give occasional design direction to other teams who maintain their own pages and want them to stay consistent with netgear.com http://netgear.com. Advisory, not production.

- Work with the app team, who own the app UI system, to keep styles, icons, colours, and typography consistent across web and app.

What we are looking for

- 4+ years designing digital products or marketing interfaces. Direct-to-consumer ecommerce or consumer tech experience is a plus, but not a requirement.

- Deep Figma skills, specifically with libraries: components, variants, auto layout, and tokens. You should be comfortable working inside an established system and maintaining its structure and documentation as you go.

- Genuine interest in AI and a habit of testing new tools as they appear. We want someone who follows how AI is developing in design, particularly the AI capabilities landing in Figma, tries them properly rather than reading about them, and brings back what actually works.

- A portfolio of shipped web work, with enough detail that we can see your reasoning and not just the final screens.
